subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should this PR's narrow `gateway.peers` session-routing model become the core cross-gateway session contract, or should it wait behind a broader federation identity/scope design?
rationale: The requested feature changes gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, and config/API surface; those choices cannot be safely settled by an automated patch review.

options.title: Design core contract first
options.body: Hold or narrow this PR until maintainers define peer identity, URL allowlisting, token scope, idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior for cross-gateway sessions.

options.title: Limit to configured trusted peers
options.body: Allow a smaller implementation only if raw `gatewayUrl` is removed from model-facing session tools and configured peers get explicit auth/TLS/replay semantics.

options.title: Route to plugin or FRD track
options.body: Keep core gateway-local for now and let the open federation tracker or a plugin bridge define the cross-gateway primitive first.

recommendation.title: Design core contract first
recommendation.body: Hold or narrow this PR until maintainers define peer identity, URL allowlisting, token scope, idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior for cross-gateway sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the session-tool and gateway URL security boundary touched by this decision.
